habitat: Pairs or small family groups in well-grassed bushveld and woodland. It walks slowly and stooped, and crouches when alarmed.
summary: A common resident. A small francolin. The male has a tawny head and neck and barred underparts. The female has a white throat bordered black and a black eyebrow extending to the upper neck. The body is light brown with fine black barring on the chest. The call is a piping ko-kwee, ko-kwee, or be-quick, be-quick. Males also give a high crowing kek, KEKekekekekekekekekek, the second note loudest. Newman’s page uses Peliperdix coqui. This file keeps Campocolinus coqui. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Shelley’s Francolin also has a white throat, but with a black surround, a white stripe through the eye, and deep red blotches on the upper breast.

calls.description: A piping ko-kwee, ko-kwee, or be-quick, be-quick, repeated continually. Males also give a loud high-pitched kek, KEKekekekekekekekekek, the second note loudest. Grade A call from Lake Nakuru, Kenya. The Limpopo grade A file is a song, so it ranks below a plain call. The filename is XC520229-2019-11-04 10_50plainbelliedcoqui.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The female is only the throat and eyebrow, which is why this needs review. Orange River Francolin is a comparison Newman names and is not in this list. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
